change: Six DEFINE_STANDARD_ALLOC scalar, array and placement operations now have actual PackedMap raw-storage bodies using existing AllocatedBytes ownership. Scalar/array requests produce aligned zeroed bytes or the native Standard_OutOfMemory payload. Placement returns the original address and placement release is a no-op.

ownership_design.allocation: BaseAllocator::common().allocate preserves zeroed aligned raw allocation and matching ownership release. No shared allocator implementation changes or new allocation registry.
ownership_design.failure: exceptions::out_of_memory preserves Standard_OutOfMemory own-message-buffer behavior and exact native what() text.
ownership_design.why_not_standard_memory: StandardMemory uses Vec<u8> alignment, unsuitable for constructing an aligned map in place.
ownership_design.why_not_typed_owner: AllocatedBox and AllocatedArray use uninitialized typed layouts, whereas these raw macro operations use Standard::Allocate zero-fill.
ownership_design.rust_adaptation: AllocatedBytes existing raw heap prepends a layout recovery header. The raw requested bytes and object lifecycle are covered; no identical physical heap footprint or C++ object ABI claim.

observations: requested length, nonnull, 16-byte alignment, zero-fill and write/read checksum
exact Standard_OutOfMemory exception type and what() for impossible requests
two live zero-byte allocations have distinct identities
placement preserves all pointer identities and bytes; mismatched delete arguments ignored
explicit scalar and three-element array placement construction, node population and reverse destruction
bucket count, map size and exact iteration sequence across signed, unsigned, narrow and bool types
actual node global allocation/release counts during successful and failing construction
caller-owned storage survives a thrown constructor and retains a tail sentinel

node_observer: Native replaces global new/delete only within explicit node tracing windows. Rust test-only System wrapper uses thread-local counters filtered to PackedMapNode layout, with no pointer registry. A u8 panic payload avoids a 16-byte string-payload allocation being misclassified as a narrow node.
typed_lifetime_proof: Native placement-new and explicit destructors are compared with existing AllocatorTypes::construct/destroy/construct_with using the raw storage returned by the new APIs. Failed construction destroys the local map and its node before retaining caller-owned storage. Strict Miri verifies pointer provenance and destruction ordering.

miri_exclusions.reason: Only the prior six positive libc-backtrace iterator tests are cfg(not(miri)); all 30 new raw-storage tests and all 264 original tests run under strict Miri.

bindings.scope: Raw class storage operation on pinned NATIVE memory policy; explicit typed lifetime is tested separately; no global API completion credit.

remaining_gaps: These are raw storage operations; typed object construction and destruction remain explicit through existing adapters.
No container ABI or compiler-generated array-cookie equivalence claim: native and Rust PackedMap object sizes differ.
Existing raw heap layout-recovery header changes physical heap footprint; allocator callback equivalence and alternate OCCT memory managers are not established here.
The canonical engine private aligned bucket adapter and transient rehash destination Vec retain their previously documented separate allocation-policy gaps.
Deterministic impossible-size failure is checked; arbitrary runtime resource exhaustion traces are not established.
No broad API inventory or global parity ledger changes are included.
